# ECON 0100 | Vignette C3 | Correctives

::: solution

# Solutions

:::

*Answers and work are shown in the red blocks.*

After the report on the connection between Glittering Gum and Starlight Sneeze, the Ministry of Magic has tasked its economics branch to develop a policy to correct the problem.

Use a graph to propose a corrective policy and how it eliminates the DWL you found in Vignette C1.

::::: solution

Policy Type: a per-unit tax. Policy Size: $6$ coins per piece of gum. Buyer’s Price $P_b$: $18$ coins. Seller’s Price $P_s$: $12$ coins. Post-Policy Quantity $Q^{\tau}$: $24$ pieces of gum. Dead Weight Loss: $0$ (Vignette C1’s $24$ coins is eliminated).

:::: {.columns gutter=1em}

::: column

From Vignette C1, demand is $P = 30 - \tfrac{1}{2} Q$ and supply is $P = 6 + \tfrac{1}{4} Q$. The market sets $30 - \tfrac{1}{2} Q = 6 + \tfrac{1}{4} Q$, so $Q = 32$ pieces of gum at $P = 14$ coins. Counting the Starlight Sneeze’s $6$ coins per piece (Vignette C1), $MSC = 12 + \tfrac{1}{4} Q$, and $30 - \tfrac{1}{2} Q = 12 + \tfrac{1}{4} Q$ gives the efficient $Q = 24$ at $P = 18$. The deadweight loss there was $\tfrac{1}{2} \times 6 \times (32 - 24) = 24$ coins.

The Starlight Sneeze is a negative externality, so the market makes too much gum. A tax equal to the external cost, $6$, makes the buyer price sit $6$ above the seller price:

$$
30 - \tfrac{1}{2} Q = \left(6 + \tfrac{1}{4} Q\right) + 6 \quad\Rightarrow\quad Q = 24
$$

Then $P_b = 30 - 12 = 18$ and $P_s = 6 + 6 = 12$. From the market’s $14$, buyers pay $4$ more and sellers keep $2$ less. The tax raises $6 \times 24 = 144$ coins.

:::

::: column

![Corrective tax on the Glittering Gum curves](data:image/svg+xml;base64,){width=100%}

:::

::::

The market now stops at $24$, the efficient quantity, so Vignette C1’s deadweight loss of $24$ is gone and the deadweight loss with the policy is $0$: each piece of gum is made only if a buyer values it at least its cost to society, sneezing included. Buyers now face marginal social cost, because the tax adds the sneeze’s $6$ to every piece.

:::::
